title: 2026 budget amendments and daytime drop-in space
subtitle: Route 98 transit expansion, climate reserve, hospital levy, bike lane snow clearing, bicentennial funding and a call on the province.
overview: Council worked through amendments to the Mayor's 2026 budget update. It added $850,000 for a daytime drop-in space {{vote:m17}} and asked the County of Wellington to cover 10% of the cost. It also approved the Route 98 transit expansion starting November 1, 2026 {{vote:m15}}.

Council first added $500,000 to the 100RE climate reserve {{vote:m3}}. Later in the day it reconsidered that decision and settled on $250,000 {{vote:m24}}. It did not restore snow clearing for on-street bike lanes {{vote:m7}}, and it did not restore Mayor and Council training funds {{vote:m6}}. The 2026 hospital levy was cut in half to $375,000 {{vote:m11}}. The bicentennial gained $47,000 for 2026 {{vote:m2}}.

Council then shortened the 30-day amendment period so it ended that day. After a break, the Mayor announced a decision not to veto any of the amendments. Council also asked the province to take back responsibility for downloaded services {{vote:m18}}. The daytime space was discussed in closed session, and the minutes record that direction was given to staff. The related motions were then moved in open session.

decisions.detail: Council added $850,000 to the 2026 operating budget, funded by the property tax levy, for daytime space, and asked the County of Wellington to contribute 10% of the cost {{vote:m17}}.
Council approved the expansion from November 1, 2026 at a 2026 cost of $642,235, with $1,385,813 added to the 2027 forecast {{vote:m15}}.
After reconsidering its earlier $500,000 decision, council set the 2026 transfer to the 100RE reserve fund, and the matching capital increase, at $250,000 {{vote:m24}}.

decisions.item: Snow clearing for on-street bike lanes
decisions.detail: Council defeated a $650,000 request to restore winter maintenance of on-street bike lanes {{vote:m7}}.
Council cut the 2026 hospital levy in half to $375,000 and directed staff to remove the 2027 reversal from the forecast {{vote:m11}}.
Council added $47,000 to the 2026 bicentennial budget, funded by the property tax levy {{vote:m2}}.
Council urged the province to take back full financial responsibility for downloaded services and to send copies of the motion to provincial and municipal bodies {{vote:m18}}.

debate: On bike lane snow clearing, supporters said the lanes are used by students and commuters, and that without clearing, cyclists would end up in traffic lanes. Others raised accessibility for mobility-device users. Opponents said the lanes are seasonal and little used in winter, and that the cost was too high. Staff said the service cannot be split by route.

On Route 98, supporters said frequency drives ridership, and that a delay would push the expansion back under the next council. They also pointed to Conestoga College students. Critics said the net cost was high compared with the expected new revenue. One councillor questioned the timing around Speedvale construction. Staff said the enhancement is not affected by the bridge work.

On the 100RE reserve, supporters said climate investment pays back through energy savings and avoided capital costs. Others said the budget total had grown by the end of the day, and the amount should be reduced. A councillor who first backed $500,000 asked for reconsideration. A $350,000 compromise was defeated.

On training funds, supporters said the money helps councillors do their jobs and benefits a new council. Opponents pointed to repeated unspent amounts in that line and to a need for restraint. A reduced $20,000 version also failed.

On the hospital levy, the Mayor said the plan keeps the full commitment by spreading it over two years. The Mayor opposed ending the levy in 2028 so the city can keep signalling to the province. That request passed {{vote:m12}}.
